title: Nominal amplitude and phase tests do not reject a fixed quadratic model in two Kepler months
abstract: We test a steady real quadratic light response to two fixed KIC 10001893 pulsations. We fit complex coefficients at the parents, difference, sum and both second harmonics in two public Kepler release-25 short-cadence months. A five-parameter response is compared with twelve free Fourier coefficients. Main aperture-flux fits give nominal chi-square tails of 0.702 in Q6 and 0.0835 in Q15. Corrected flux gives the same main decision. Four of 24 dependent settings have tails below 0.05, all with two-day noise blocks and few covariance blocks. Thus the phase test gives no stable rejection of this restricted model. Gaussian coefficient simulations test only a fixed-covariance approximation. Estimated noise coverage, unresolved modes, fixed frequencies and source mixing limit the result. No planet or new signal is confirmed. Code, aggregate results, input hashes and external retrieval steps are included.

display.caption: Nominal fit tails depend on residual block length in two short-cadence months. The noise covariance coverage is untested.
